newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China deports four Taiwan reporters.
newsitem.headline: China deports four Taiwan reporters.

text.p: China has deported four Taiwanese television reporters who were covering a controversial power plant project by Taiwan's top industrial enterprise, Formosa Plastics, state media said on Wednesday.
The four reporters were detained late on Tuesday when they tried to film the construction site of the US$3 billion power station in coastal Chinese Fujian province, state media said.

Formosa had triggered a weekend of uncertainty by saying it was going ahead with the project in defiance of Taipei's wishes, but apparently backed down on Monday, pledging to respect the government's policy and abandon the giant investment.
Taipei worries that its prosperous economy could become too dependent on China, leaving it politically vulnerable.
State-run Central News Agency quoted sources as saying the four reporters were told to get permission from Formosa chairman Wang Yung-ching before shooting footage of the plant.
The reporters, two from a Taiwan state television and two from a private cable television, were brought to a private guest house and questioned by local authorities.
Fujian government officials said they had booked tickets for the reporters and asked them to leave the country.
Beijing has regarded Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and pledges to retake the island eventually, by force if necessary.
